title: Anaemia of CKD

steps.tx: The central pathogenic driver of anemia in chronic kidney disease is relative **erythropoietin** (**EPO**) deficiency resulting from progressive loss of specialized peritubular interstitial fibroblastic cells. Termed **REP cells**, these oxygen-sensing interstitial fibroblasts transdifferentiate into non-secretory alpha-smooth muscle actin-positive myofibroblasts, blunting physiological erythropoietic hormone synthesis in response to tissue hypoxia.

steps.tx: Systemic inflammation in advanced CKD induces sustained hepatic synthesis of the acute-phase peptide **hepcidin**, triggering profound **functional iron deficiency**. Circulating hepcidin binds directly to the basolateral iron exporter **ferroportin** on duodenal enterocytes and reticuloendothelial macrophages, inducing its internalisation and lysosomal degradation to trap iron within storage pools.

steps.tx: Under international **KDIGO** guidelines, iron deficiency in patients with chronic kidney disease is defined by a transferrin saturation (**TSAT**) <= **30%** accompanied by a serum **ferritin** <= **500** ng/mL. Intravenous or oral **iron supplementation** must be administered to replete iron stores prior to initiating or escalating erythropoiesis-stimulating agent therapy.
steps.say: Under international KDIGO guidelines, iron deficiency in patients with chronic kidney disease is defined by a transferrin saturation of 30% or less accompanied by a serum ferritin of 500 ng/mL or less. Intravenous or oral iron supplementation must be administered to replete iron stores prior to initiating or escalating erythropoiesis-stimulating agent therapy.

steps.tx: Landmark randomized clinical trials including **CHOIR**, **CREATE**, and **TREAT** established that completely normalizing hemoglobin levels (> **13** g/dL) using high-dose ESAs significantly escalates risks of fatal and non-fatal **stroke**, severe cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and vascular access thrombosis without improving survival.
steps.say: Landmark randomized clinical trials established that completely normalizing hemoglobin levels above 13 g/dL using high-dose ESAs significantly escalates risks of fatal and non-fatal stroke, severe cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and vascular access thrombosis without improving survival.

left.title: Normal Target Trials (> 13 g/dL)
points: Increased risk of ischemic stroke and death

right.title: Current Conservative Target
points: Reduces red blood cell transfusion needs

steps.tx: Current clinical consensus guidelines recommend initiating **ESA therapy** (**epoetin alfa**, darbepoetin alfa, or methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta) only when hemoglobin falls below **10** g/dL. Clinical titration aims strictly to maintain circulating hemoglobin between **10.0** and **11.5** g/dL, while deliberately avoiding levels exceeding **11.5** to **12.0** g/dL.

steps.tx: Orally active **HIF-PHIs** (**roxadustat**, vadadustat, daprodustat) inhibit hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase enzymes, preventing the oxygen-dependent degradation of **HIF-alpha**. Stabilized HIF heterodimers translocate to the nucleus, simultaneously stimulating endogenous renal and hepatic erythropoietin production, enhancing intestinal iron absorption via DMT1, and actively suppressing circulating **hepcidin**.

right.title: Recombinant ESA Injections
points: No direct regulatory effect on hepcidin

steps.tx: Acquired **Pure red cell aplasia** (**PRCA**) represents a rare immunological disaster caused by circulating neutralizing anti-erythropoietin antibodies targeting exogenous and endogenous EPO. Diagnosis is confirmed by sudden severe transfusion-dependent anemia, profound reticulocytopenia with an absolute reticulocyte count below **10,000**/mcL, and severe isolated absence of erythroblasts on **bone marrow** aspirate.

right.title: Therapeutic Strategy
points: Strictly avoid switching to other ESAs
Provide packed red blood cell transfusions

steps.tx: True **Erythropoietin resistance** (hyporesponsiveness) is diagnosed when patients require persistently escalating ESA doses without achieving target hemoglobin concentrations. The most prevalent contributing clinical etiologies include undetected absolute **iron deficiency**, chronic occult **infection**, underlying hematologic malignancies, ongoing occult gastrointestinal blood loss, severe hyperparathyroidism, and inadequate hemodialysis clearance.

nodes.label: Failure to achieve target Hb despite high ESA
Screen for iron deficiency and occult inflammation
Correct underlying infection, bleeding, or hyperparathyroidism
